findings.title: diffstorm/cb, two defects (fixed upstream)
findings.defects: 1. the overwrite flag can switch itself on (all platforms); 2. the consumer lacks acquire ordering (multi-core targets)
findings.found_by: the verified-libs stress harness and GenMC (RC11 model checking)

notes.text: AndersKaloer uses plain variables; this build happens to keep a safe store order, which the language does not guarantee. Its queue function overwrites when full; the adapter checks for space first.

diffstorm up to `547d0812` had two defects, found by GenMC and a host reproducer: the 1-byte overwrite flag was accessed with 32-bit loads/stores, so uninitialised padding could turn overwrite mode on (silent data loss), and the consumer lacked acquire ordering (matters across cores). The stress test passed only because the test object is in zeroed memory. Reported on 2026-11-08; the maintainer fixed both the same day (`91ae20b`). The row is `11e05d60`: GenMC passes, the reproducer gives the correct result, and the board stress (single, block, flash and SRAM, 2026-11-09) has 0 errors. The maintainer agreed on 2026-11-09 to publication before the 90 days were over. See the finding.

libs.name: Nordic nrf_ringbuf
libs.boards_only_why: Nordic's licence allows use with Nordic chips only; the nRF5 SDK is a zip from nordicsemi.com, pinned by SHA-256 (nrf5-sdk.lock)

mp.via: Topology::MPSC, SPMC, MPMC (interrupts masked around push and/or pop)

notes.text: pxq uses `volatile` for its documented contract (ISR ↔ main loop on one core). Under the C11 model that is a data race by definition, so it is checked against its contract (the one-core contract check), not with the plain C11 check.

pxq ⚠: its MPSC, SPMC and MPMC modes mask interrupts, so they are for one core; with the producers or consumers on the Pico 2's two cores they give errors, and reserve/commit starves (not counted: not a documented use; see the validation report). On the NUCLEO-H723ZG its indices share a cache line with its data; a DMA can only use it in non-cacheable memory (DMA report).
Without user-supplied `RB_ATOMIC_START/END` macros wizard97 is not ISR-safe, as its own header warns. With them: 0 errors (wizard97 + PRIMASK macros).
